text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] high severity: gpu-prefill OOMs causing container restarts in cluster=us-east-1-prod (group: model-serving). sample: container=svc-model-3f2, node=gpu-12-prod, reason=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY

jamie_oncall: acked. paging SRE + ML. tagging @raul_eng @eva_ml @lee_platform

raul_eng: I'm on it. looking at the kube events and logs now. initial hypothesis: large-context prefill from very long requests + prefetch enabled, exceeding reserved GPU mem during prefill.

eva_ml: we saw similar before with the long-window customers. which model & quantization?

raul_eng: model=redwood-v1-large, quant=8bit, batcher shows multiple concurrent prefill ops coalescing. example log: 
```
2026-03-16T21:17:03Z ERROR: cudaRuntime: out of memory while allocating 348 MB
prefill: tokens=120k, concurrent_prefills=6, kv_cache_alloc=~18GB
container restart: kubelet killed container due to OOM
```

jamie_oncall: customer impact? any 5xx spike?

nina_custops: metrics dashboard shows a small spike in 5xx from 21:16-21:22 ~0.8% of traffic. one large customer (acct ACME_CORP) reported slow/no responses on batch jobs. logging their request ids now.

lee_platform: quick mitigation options: 1) disable prefetch/prefill (feature flag) 2) throttle concurrent prefill to 1 per GPU 3) fallback to smaller model variant or CPU coldmodel for long-context heavy requests 4) cordon / drain offending node for immediate containment.

raul_eng: implementing (1) + (2) now. applying flag: 
```
curl -X POST https://console/api/featureflags -d '{"prefill.enabled":false,"prefill.concurrency":1}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP'
```

jamie_oncall: do it in prod and dedicate to affected AZ only? we want minimal blast radius.

lee_platform: rolling the flag to us-east-1-prod first. scheduling a controlled ramp-down across pods: set maxSurge=0, maxUnavailable=1 for the rollout.

raul_eng: flag applied to us-east-1-prod, restarting affected deployments with graceful drain. monitoring logs.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] flag change detected by deploy-bot: prefill.enabled=false for rollout=us-east-1-prod (triggered by jamie_oncall).

eva_ml: also posting a guideline: for long-context workloads we should route to quantized-cpu-smaller or use KV-caching on ingestion. creating a quick eval to estimate quality drop if we fallback.

nina_custops: ACME_CORP impacted requests identified: 4 failing job runs between 21:16-21:20. opened support ticket #INC-6489 and notified their CS rep.

raul_eng: memory error rate dropping after flag flip. current OOM count decreased to 0 over last 3 minutes. containers stabilized.

jamie_oncall: nice. next: postmortem owners, followups, and customer comms. who owns short-term routing rule to prevent long-prefill from hitting GPU pool?

lee_platform: I'll add a routing policy: add a prefill-length cutoff at the gateway to divert >50k-token prefill to a specialized pool (coldmodel or staged CPU fallback). I'll create the config change and a canary.

eva_ml: I'll run evals on a small prompt set to compare redwood-v1-large -> smaller-variant and validate quality. putting a regression alert in Optimize.

raul_eng: for the P1 postmortem: collecting logs, pod core dumps, and perf profiles. saving kernel dmesg and nvcrash artifacts at s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/1871112222/.

nina_custops: customer update draft: "We experienced a short disruption due to large-context requests causing GPU memory exhaustion during prefill. We applied an immediate mitigation (disabled prefetch + throttled prefill) and traffic is stable. Our engineering team is working on permanent routing and fallback changes. We will follow up with a full incident report and any recommended request-size limits." please review.

jamie_oncall: looks good. add ETA for next update in 60 mins. assign postmortem owner: @raul_eng. action items:
- (raul_eng) gather artifacts and timeline
- (lee_platform) implement routing cutoff and canary by EOD
- (eva_ml) eval fallback quality and tune quantization by EOD+1
- (nina_custops) customer comms and ticket updates

lee_platform: one more note: long-running prefill + streaming responses = prefill never freed in time on multi-tenant GPUs. we'll add an eviction policy for KV caches > XGB and a hard timeout for prefill operations.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE] Incident state changed to mitigated. OOMs stopped, services stabilized. Creating incident record and paging postmortem workflow.

jamie_oncall: closing live page. handing off to postmortem owners. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

raul_eng: leaving a short runbook entry: "If GPU OOMs during prefill: 1) disable prefetch 2) throttle prefill concurrency 3) divert >50k prefill to fallback pool 4) cordon node if restarts persist". will commit to repo after review.

nina_custops: updated ticket #INC-6489 and emailed ACME_CORP with root-cause and short remediation.

eva_ml: adding regression alert to Optimize and a prompt-set to monitor long-window quality after fallback.

lee_platform: creating follow-up RFC for prefill admission control and longer-term KV eviction strategy.

jamie_oncall: great work. incident closed for on-call. postmortem owners will schedule a 1-hour scrub tomorrow.

(END THREAD)
